لَيْلَةٌ وَمِدٌ : (L, K:) and ↓ وَمِدَةٌ , (T, M, A, L, K,) which latter is the more common, (TA,) A night of وَمَد, i. e., intense heat, &c., as explained above. (T, M, A, L, K.) One also says يَوْمٌ وَمِدٌ: but not so commonly. (M, L.) ―
-b2- هُوَ عَلَيْهِ وَمِدٌ (tropical:) He is angry with him. (A.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
